title: SteadyFlow token odometer: microbenchmark suite for sustained & burst TPS
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build and maintain the SteadyFlow token odometer microbenchmark suite for core models. The goal is a reproducible harness that measures sustained tokens/sec under steady-state and microburst conditions, tracks p95 token latency regressions, and fingerprints regressions deterministically across model versions and kernel selections. This ticket covers test design, CI integration, result digesting, dashboard plumbing, and a lightweight statistical regression detector that tolerates noise from stochastic sampling and KV cache warmup.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run steady-state token emit tests for 1, 5, and 15 minute windows with configurable sequence-length distributions
Microburst mode: support 5s/30s/2m bursts with configurable base load and burst multiplier
p95 and p99 latency computed per-window and persisted to perfstore; p95 drift alert triggered if exceeds baseline by configured relative threshold
Regression detector runs in CI and emits a concise failure summary with top contributing traces and reproducible replay seed
Dashboards updated: per-model throughput, p95 trendline, per-run annotation for kernel/quantization profile
Artifacts (raw token traces, KV cache warmup profile, CPU/GPU utilization) uploaded to the benchmark S3 bucket and linked from the CI job
tasks: Design test harness API and YAML schema for test scenarios (steady, burst, ramp, seq-dist)
Implement runner that drives HTTP/GRPC endpoints with request pacing and jitter injection
Add KV cache priming and warmup hooks to separate cold vs warm metrics
Extend existing perfstore schema to accept per-run p50/p95/p99, token/sec, tail-latency histogram
Integrate regression detector into nightly CI with a gated threshold configuration
Create Grafana dashboard panels and a short-run summary view for on-call use
Add reproducible seed and request recorder to enable reliable replay for flaky regressions
Document recommended baseline configs for core models and provide compare scripts for release engineers
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Khan: Initial write-up. Goal is to reduce noisy false-positives in p95 alerts that we've seen previously by accounting for KV warmup and sequence-length distribution.

2026-02-24 - Mateo Ruiz: Spike completed exploring pacing implementations. Found that naive fixed-interval pacing coalesces under load; switching to Poisson arrival pacing plus small jitter reduces request alignment artifacts.
